title: Maccheroni al Ferretto
subtitle: Hand-rolled pasta tubes in a slow-cooked tomato and pork ragu
excerpt: Thick pasta tubes shaped around a thin rod, sauced with a rich pork ragu. A Calabrian Sunday dish that takes time but rewards patience.
sourceNotes: Calabrian tradition of hand-rolled pasta with ferretto rod, combined with a slow pork-based sugo.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the ragu separately. Defrost overnight and reheat gently. Roll fresh pasta on the day.
recipe.batchNotes: Double the ragu and freeze half. The pasta dough is easiest in single batches.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make the ragu a day ahead. Rest and roll the pasta dough on the day of serving.

content.text: Maccheroni al ferretto are rough-edged pasta tubes shaped by hand around a thin knitting needle or skewer. The pork ragu underneath is cooked low and slow until it clings to every ridge. Keep the dough firm so the tubes hold their shape when you roll them.
Mix the flour and salt in a large bowl. Add water a little at a time and knead into a firm dough. It should not be sticky. Cover and rest for 30 minutes.
Heat the olive oil in a large saucepan. Brown the pork pieces well on all sides. Do this in batches so the pan stays hot. Remove and set aside.
Soften the onion in the same pan for 8 minutes. Add the garlic and cook for 2 minutes more.
Pour in the red wine. Let it simmer for 2 minutes. Add the tinned tomatoes and return the pork. Season well. Cook on a very low heat for 75 minutes, stirring every 15 minutes.

Pinch off walnut-sized pieces of dough. Press each piece around a thin skewer or knitting needle. Roll it firmly on the board with your palm. Slide the tube off carefully. Repeat until all the dough is used.
Bring a large pan of salted water to the boil. Cook the pasta for 4 to 5 minutes until tender but with a little bite.
Stir the basil through the ragu. Drain the pasta and toss it with the ragu. Serve with grated parmesan.

items.symptom: The pasta tubes split when I roll them.
items.cause: The dough is too dry or has not rested long enough.
items.fix: Work in a few drops of water and rest the dough for another 15 minutes before rolling.

items.symptom: The ragu catches on the bottom of the pan.
items.cause: The heat is too high or there is not enough liquid.
items.fix: Add a splash of water and turn the heat to its lowest setting.

items.symptom: The pasta sticks together on the board.
items.cause: The shaped tubes are touching each other.
items.fix: Dust the board with flour and spread the tubes in a single layer so they do not touch.
